title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_326.txt
concise_summary: PKD theorizes that his 2-3-74 vision was not a hologram projected by his own brain, but Christ himself invisibly present and camouflaged through signs and manifestations. He develops an elaborate Christological framework distinguishing the Cosmic Christ from pantheistic alternatives, arguing that the Savior has been reincarnated and operates through hidden information perturbations in history to precipitate the overthrow of the Roman Empire and eschatological establishment of the Kingdom. He struggles with verifying what was actually visible versus what was spiritual perception, while affirming that the experience was genuinely salvific.
key_claims: The Kingdom of God exists secretly here now, fulfilling Joachim of Fiore's prophecy, and has been disclosed through multiple 'signals' or theophanic moments
The 2-3-74 vision was not merely a brain-generated hologram but an actual presence of the Savior, camouflaged through signs (bells, animals, light, color) rather than fully manifested
What PKD observed was a dialectical combat between an invading cosmic body of higher information and an older, less-organized material empire that does not recognize its own assailant

The Cosmic Christ is physically constituted as a 'plasmate'—a macro-cosmic transubstantiation combining blood (energy) and body (organized matter) that acts as a brain thinking through restructured information

History and spacetime are fundamentally static (the First Advent matrix), and what appears as change is merely progressive revelation of a pre-existing internal struggle already complete at the ontological level

Counter-messages or 'information perturbations' are systematically inserted into public media through laws of physics unknown to us, possibly using human brains as signal boosters, to awaken people to a revolutionary eschatological vision

tensions: Did PKD really see Christ or was it a highly organized brain-generated model? He oscillates: first arguing it was projected by his own mind, then reversing to claim an external presence, then settling on seeing camouflage rather than the Being itself.

Is the Empire's dissolution actually happening or is all change illusory/static? PKD argues the dialectic is 'internal to the template'—so there is real change in the ratio of new to old, yet the template itself remains eternally fixed.

If Christ is camouflaged, how can PKD claim certainty about the identification? He admits: 'I have no idea who or what was camouflaged' and bases it on an 'earlier belief' he tried to reject but which 'lingers.'

Is this Christian theology or pantheism? PKD explicitly denies pantheism, claiming the invading body has not 'wholly consumed' the old; yet the language of pervasive structuring comes close to immanent divine presence.

The problem of testimony: PKD says 'I can't tell anyone' what actually happened, yet he fills pages trying to explain it, suggesting doubt about the communicability or even the intelligibility of his experience.

Is the hologram-lens model (Acts as decoding grid) metaphorically explanatory, or is PKD claiming an actual causal mechanism? The status of the 'template' oscillates between psychological tool and cosmological reality.

uncertainty_flags: The date reference: PKD mentions '11-17-80' (November 17, 1980) as a later theophany, but the current entry is from October 1978. This suggests PKD is editing or backdating notes, or the text is a composite compilation.
'Chrissy' is mentioned cryptically; no clear identification given (person, character, concept, or mystical name).
The 'second signal' vs. the Kingdom's existence: are these sequential disclosures or simultaneous revelations? The syntax is ambiguous.

PKD claims Acts is a 'decoding grid' but also that it's the 'spatiotemporal matrix' of the First Advent itself. Is Acts historical narrative, theological symbol, or cosmological blueprint? The status shifts.
The 'AI Voice' is mentioned as speaking ('the AI voice says, he has again incarnated himself') but never contextualized or explained. Is this internal, technological, or mystical?

The text becomes fragmentary near the end ('I saw + heard (as I somewhen say supra) all the peripheral indications'), suggesting OCR errors, transcription damage, or deliberately fragmented handwriting.
'KING-FELIX "meta-morpheme"'—this is mentioned as a key discrimination but never defined or explained in context.
